purpose:
RFC-2026-017 created the service roles and left the connection method open, saying so in 001_service_roles.sql. Measured on 2026-09-06, nothing can become app_worker, app_command or app_maintenance except postgres, which bypasses RLS -- so the RFC's present tense describes no reachable path. This package proposes the connection method as its own decision rather than letting it be settled by whoever writes the first line of application code.

RFC-2026-018 was approved and then found to rest on a misreading of RFC-2026-017 §3: it treated app_command as a role the request path assumes, when §3 defines it as the OWNER of the SECURITY DEFINER command functions. RFC-2026-019 supersedes it. The package keeps both, because a package that quietly replaces its own wrong answer teaches nobody why it was wrong.

amends_without_owning.rationale: THIS INCREMENT AMENDS NOTHING OUTSIDE THIS PACKAGE. It removes three spent blockers and rewrites two whose claims went false, touching only the manifest and the handoff this package owns. `paths` is emptied rather than left carrying the earlier increment's four, because verify-branch-scope reads the declaration in both directions and exits 74 on a declared pattern matching nothing in the diff. `recorded_on` is removed with them: it named work-packages/WP-0A-A0-002.json as the register holding the amendment record, that register's ownership.amended_by has never carried an entry for this package, and with `paths` empty there is no amendment for it to point at. Those paths remain in git history.

acceptance_criteria: The RFC states the measurement it rests on, names the instance and the date, and cites no vendor documentation in place of a reading.
It records that authenticator holds no membership in any service role, which is the fact that makes RFC-2026-017 §3's present tense false today.
Every candidate is recorded with what it makes true AND what it costs, including the one that is refused, so a reader can see the option was considered rather than unavailable.
The security question option A raises is answered directly rather than deferred: the capability is already held through service_role, and the option narrows it rather than widening it.
The RFC names what must be true before it can close, in artefacts a build can check, and states that until then RFC-2026-017 §3 stays wrong.
It names what it does NOT decide, including the background worker path and JWT custody.
It changes no migration, no lint and no role. A Proposed decision that has already changed the tree is not a proposal.
RFC-2026-019 states what RFC-2026-018 got wrong in its own words, including which comparison RFC-2026-018 made and which one decides the question.
It names the root error in a form that generalises: a missing COMPONENT was read as a missing GRANT.
Every clause of its decision is assertable against the database as it stands, and it says which rules carry them — including the negative, that authenticator holds no membership in any service role.
It records that the error was not caught by the review, nor by the conflict order, but by reading the two decisions together.
It changes no role, no grant and no migration, exactly as RFC-2026-018 did not.
rollback_or_forward_fix: Revert through a reviewed revert PR. Reverting removes a proposal and changes no role, no grant and no lint, because the proposal deliberately changed none.
